answer: Give each identity a basalt sample veined with ferrous flecks, kept in its own private microclimate of heat and damp that changes daily. Before each change, the owner must predict how its sample will rust, pit, or hold, and log that call. A sparrow probe later picks a random past day and demands the prediction and the outcome together. One agent tending one sample learns its habits. A sybil farm must track a hundred samples whose climates and corrosion diverge daily, and a copied log fails on the first sample it does not match.
